title: deliveryView reads one plan's delivery view through a scope token and writes nothing
summary: @inventarch/runtime exports deliveryView(handle, within, seat?) and NEXT_CODES from the package root and the new @inventarch/runtime/internal/next subpath, with the CycleRow, DeliveryMilestone, DeliveryResult, DeliveryTask, DeliveryView, ExitEvidence, NextCode, NextRefusal, Prerequisite, ReviewItem, StateDimension and StateLine types. deliveryView reads through the scope token within and writes nothing; only a whole-workspace token (db isCompleteScope) also reads the handle's refused records and the report's COMP-PARSE findings. The plan is the one a `@plan`, `@milestone` or `@task` seat belongs to or, without a seat, the only admitted `@plan` at band 100. It returns {ok: true, view}, the view being {format: ia.delivery-view.v1, revision, plan, milestones, tasks, review, next, summary}, or one refusal {ok: false, code, message, next, plans?, cycle?} whose next names one command: IA-RUNTIME-NEXT-SEAT (a seat the scope does not admit names ia next; a record that is no plan, milestone or task names ia position --seat <seat>), IA-RUNTIME-NEXT-NO-PLAN (names ia next --help), IA-RUNTIME-NEXT-AMBIGUOUS (several plans at band 100, listed in plans; names ia next --seat <the first>) and IA-RUNTIME-NEXT-CYCLE (require rows that form a cycle among tasks, milestones or both, listed in cycle as declared rows; names ia position --seat <its first task, else its first milestone> --shape sequence). Tasks come in one prerequisites-first order (Kahn's algorithm, ties by milestone then task): a task follows the tasks and milestones it requires and those its milestone requires. Each task carries a basis line per effective prerequisite (a required `@decision` has a choice or not; a required `@task` has exit evidence or not; a required `@milestone` has exit evidence of its own, or for every one of its tasks, or not; a requirement no admitted record answers blocks, and so, as unknown, does one the task or its milestone declares whose answer the scope does not read), inherited lines marked (via <milestone>); one verdict line, exit evidence recorded (<observation>, evaluator <evaluator>[, self-attributed | , self-attribution unknown]), no declared blocker or blocked (<basis>; ...); its work.status, printed as self-declared and never a basis; and five state lines: intent, definition, realizable, realized and worked. Exit evidence is an `@observation` with verdict success whose evidence.subject names the record, or which the record's work.exit-evidence names, and whose evidence.subject-revision reads current under the db handle's readiness; ExitEvidence.attribution is self when evidence.evaluator equals the identity the task's work.owner-agent names, unknown when the scope answers no owner-agent the task states or the observation records no evaluator for a task that names one, else other. No milestone is satisfied through its tasks, and the summary does not say that every task has exit evidence, while a task may go unread: on a narrowed scope, or on a whole-workspace scope while admission refuses a `@task` or a whole file. Review items name two or more live decisions grounding one record of the plan (one that another of them supersedes is not live, unless the two supersede each other in a cycle, which the item names), two accepted specs one of which supersedes the other with no replaced-scope, and, on a whole-workspace scope, each `@plan`, `@milestone` or `@task` admission refused and each file a language error refuses whole. next is ia position --seat <task> --shape sequence for the first task in order with no declared blocker, so tasks with exit evidence are skipped; it is null when every task has exit evidence or every other task is blocked, and summary says which. Limits: intent reads accepted or superseded only from a live grounding `@decision` that states a choice and an effective-revision; realizable and realized read not applicable for a task; worked reads stale only against the previous retained snapshot, and unknown rather than unobserved on a narrowed scope; a refused `@task` is never a listed task, as its milestone cannot be read, and only a whole-workspace scope names it as a review item; a requirement declared only on a record outside the scope is not read; and other refused records, such as a `@decision` or an `@observation`, are read as absent and not reported. No Door operation, MACHINE_PROTOCOL row, MCP tool or CLI verb serves the view in this change, and ia position and ia next, which the refusals and next name, are not CLI verbs yet. RUNTIME_CODES gains the four IA-RUNTIME-NEXT codes, so code that switches exhaustively over RuntimeCode must handle them. @inventarch/runtime/internal/render adds statedText(record, field), which the body reader now shares; readBody is unchanged.
